The keyboard shortcut tool TextExpander, known for its extreme usefulness, has now launched a free plan, allowing users to access its core Snippets feature on Mac, iPhone, iPad, Windows and Chrome. Here are the details.

TextExpander launches free plan

I have written before that TextExpander is one of the first applications I install after buying a new Mac.

Over the years, I have built up approximately 200 Snippets (TextExpander's term for text abbreviations that can automatically expand into pre-written text), most of which I use frequently, such as for quickly replying to emails, filling out forms, preparing Podcast outlines, reading sponsor advertisements, writing show notes, and so on.

Although macOS's native text replacement support has been improving, features such as variable support, conditional paragraphs, nested Snippets and math macros make TextExpander an indispensable tool for me.

TextExpander recently launched a free plan. According to the company and 9to5Mac, it allows users to store 5 active Snippets, unlimited library storage, unlimited text expansions, and up to 5 team members. The free plan also supports Mac, iPhone, iPad, Windows and Chrome simultaneously, with the same Snippet library kept in sync across different devices.

Honestly, the limit of 5 Snippets may feel a bit restrictive, especially since the free plan only allows swapping out one active Snippet every two weeks.

Nevertheless, this plan can serve as a great way to get started, keeping shorter and simpler text replacements on macOS while reserving TextExpander for longer or more complex Snippets.

To learn more about TextExpander's free plan, please follow this link.
